say.text: Right. A previous operation makes adhesions likely; none points to the hernial orifices first.
Trap: adhesions are not the answer everywhere. PYQs keyed hernia for India, and a virgin abdomen has no scar to form them.
Trap: adhesions need an operation behind them. With none, check every hernial orifice first.
Two men have small bowel obstruction. Ravi had an appendicectomy at 20. Imran, a 33-year-old farmer, has never had surgery.
Which pairing of causes fits best?

choices.label: Ravi: adhesions. Imran: a hernia first, then tumour
Adhesions in both, as they are the commonest cause everywhere
Adhesions for Ravi, a congenital band for Imran, as any adult fits

say.text: Trap: the familiar film is not the confirming test. In a child, ultrasound is the investigation of choice.
Trap: not every intussusception goes to theatre. A stable child without peritonitis gets enema reduction first.
Right. Ultrasound confirms, and a stable child without peritonitis gets enema reduction. An adult, with a lead point, is resected.
An 8-month-old has screaming spells with drawn-up legs and red currant jelly stool. He is resuscitated and stable, with no peritonitis.
Which confirms the diagnosis, and what comes next?

choices.label: Plain X-ray as the definitive test, then theatre
Barium meal to confirm, then theatre
Ultrasound shows a target sign; image-guided enema reduction follows

say.text: Trap: folds crossing the full width are valvulae of small bowel. Folds that stop short are haustra of large bowel.
Trap: 9 cm is the caecal limit. The colon limit is 6 cm and small bowel 3 cm.
Right. Haustra that do not cross, a peripheral position and a colon over 6 cm all say large bowel.
A supine film shows peripheral loops with folds that stop short of the full width. The transverse colon measures 7 cm.
What does it show?

choices.label: Dilated small bowel, because folds mark small bowel
Normal colon, as the upper limit is 9 cm
Dilated large bowel: haustra, and above the 6 cm limit

say.text: Trap: commonest does not mean riskiest. The femoral hernia, with its narrow rigid neck, strangulates most.
Right. Femoral is the groin hernia most likely to strangulate.
Trap: Richter's traps part of the wall, so it can strangulate with flatus and no distension.
A surgeon teaches about groin hernias in a 68-year-old woman and a 30-year-old man. Which statement is right?

choices.label: The indirect inguinal hernia strangulates most, being the commonest
Femoral: narrow, rigid neck gives the highest risk
Richter's hernia is safe unless obstruction is complete, with vomiting and distension

say.text: Trap: that is the sigmoid pathway. Caecal volvulus usually fails detorsion and is resected.
Right. Caecal volvulus gets a right hemicolectomy, and the kidney-shaped caecum separates it from the coffee bean of sigmoid.
Trap: coffee bean is the sigmoid sign. A kidney-shaped caecum in the left upper quadrant is caecal volvulus.
A 71-year-old woman is stable. CT shows a whirl sign. The film shows a kidney-shaped caecum in the left upper quadrant.
What is the best operation?

choices.label: Colonoscopic detorsion and a flatus tube, then discharge
Coffee bean sign, so sigmoid; endoscopic detorsion

say.text: Trap: theatre does not come first. Fluids, potassium, NG tube and catheter come before any decision.
Right. Resuscitate first. A negative screen allows a non-operative trial.
Trap: the trial is not a replacement for resuscitation. Drip and suck is how the trial is run.
A 55-year-old is dry, vomiting, with pulse 112 and a distended abdomen. There is no peritonitis and the screen is negative.
Which plan is best?

choices.label: Theatre now, with fluids started on the table
Drip and suck first, then decide on a trial
Start the 72-hour trial without fluids, since he is stable

say.text: Trap: 24 hours and 72 hours are different clocks. Contrast in the colon by 24 hours predicts resolution.
Right. Contrast in the colon within 24 hours predicts resolution. The trial limit is about 72 hours.
Trap: 24 hours is the contrast marker, not the trial limit. That is about 72 hours.
A 70-year-old on a trial for adhesive obstruction has no strangulation signs. Water-soluble contrast was given. A film at 24 hours shows contrast in the caecum and rectum.
What does this mean?

choices.label: Nothing yet; contrast means nothing until 72 hours
Trial limit is 24 hours; operate if not resolved

say.text: Right. Constant pain, fever, tachycardia and localised tenderness override the trial.
Trap: pain that turns constant is not settling. Constant pain with tachycardia and fever reads as strangulation.
Trap: the trial applies only when the screen is negative. Strangulation signs skip it.
A 49-year-old woman with adhesive obstruction has had colicky pain for two days. Now the pain has become a constant ache. Pulse 122, temperature 38.2, tender in the left iliac fossa.
What do you do?

choices.label: Resuscitate, then operate; this is strangulation
Continue the trial; the pain is settling
Carry on to 72 hours, then review

say.text: Trap: timelines differ by level. Early profuse vomiting with minimal distension is a high small bowel block.
Right. In large bowel block constipation is early and vomiting is late. In high small bowel block it is the reverse.
Trap: constipation is late in small bowel block but early in large, as the distal bowel empties first.

Which patient fits a low large bowel block: a 60-year-old with marked flank distension, no flatus since yesterday and no vomiting yet, or a 40-year-old who vomits profusely with a flat abdomen and still passes flatus?

choices.label: The second: vomiting comes first at every level
The first: absolute constipation and marked distension come early, vomiting late

say.text: Trap: bowel sounds are absent in paralytic ileus. Hyperactive sounds belong to mechanical obstruction.
Right. Hypokalaemia is the commonest metabolic cause of ileus, treated non-operatively with correction and drip and suck.
Trap: the trial is for mechanical adhesive obstruction. Here, fix the potassium first.
On day 4 after laparotomy a man is distended and vomiting. The abdomen is silent. Potassium is 2.8. There is no fever.
What fits, and what is first?

choices.label: Mechanical block, as bowel sounds are always hyperactive in obstruction
Ileus: correct potassium, drip and suck
Start a 72-hour trial for adhesions and leave potassium

say.text: Level and setting give the cause, strangulation overrides the wait, and resuscitation comes before theatre.
The cards that follow carry these into new cases.
Trap: an adult usually has a lead point, often a tumour, so resection is needed.
Trap: a stent bridges left-sided disease. Right-sided cancer gets right hemicolectomy with primary anastomosis.
Trap: colorectal carcinoma is commonest. Diverticular disease and volvulus follow.
Right. The operation follows the site of the cancer; carcinoma is the commonest cause of adult large bowel block.
Which statement about large bowel and intussusception in adults is true?

choices.label: Adult intussusception is reduced by enema, as in a child
Obstructing right-sided cancer is stented as standard
Diverticular disease is the commonest cause of adult large bowel block
Right-sided obstructing cancer: right hemicolectomy, primary anastomosis

say.text: Trap: carcinoma, stricture and intussusception lie in the wall. Sort by the bowel wall, not by name.
Right. Bands, hernia and volvulus are extramural; the wall holds carcinoma, strictures and intussusception.
Trap: a stricture sits in the wall and is intramural. Name does not sort causes; relation to the wall does.
Which of these is NOT an intramural cause of obstruction?

cards.q: PYQ key versus current practice: most common cause of adult small bowel obstruction in India?
cards.a: PYQs expected an obstructed or strangulated hernia in India and developing countries; adhesions are the most common cause in the West and where surgery is common.

cards.q: Which cardinal feature comes early in a large bowel obstruction?
cards.a: Absolute constipation, because the distal bowel empties first; vomiting is late and distension is marked.

cards.q: Constant severe pain with tachycardia and guarding: what does it mean?
cards.a: Strangulation, from venous block then ischaemia; it needs urgent surgery after resuscitation.

cards.q: Small bowel or large bowel on a plain film: which marker?
cards.a: Valvulae conniventes cross the full width in small bowel; haustra do not cross in large bowel. Upper normal diameters: small bowel 3 cm, colon 6 cm, caecum 9 cm.

cards.q: First test and definitive test for small bowel obstruction in an adult?
cards.a: Plain abdominal X-ray is the first test; contrast-enhanced CT abdomen is the investigation of choice.

cards.q: Coffee bean sign on a plain film?
cards.a: Sigmoid volvulus. Caecal volvulus gives a kidney-shaped caecum in the left upper quadrant.

cards.q: Adhesive obstruction: what does contrast in the colon within 24 hours predict, and when is the trial's limit?
cards.a: Resolution without surgery; the trial's limit is about 72 hours, and strangulation, hernia or closed loop skip the trial.

cards.q: Which groin hernia is most likely to strangulate, and what is Richter's hernia?
cards.a: The femoral hernia, with its narrow rigid neck. Richter's traps part of the wall, so it strangulates without complete obstruction.

cards.q: Intussusception: enema reduction or resection, child versus adult?
cards.a: A child without peritonitis gets image-guided enema reduction; an adult usually has a lead point, often a tumour, and is resected.

cards.q: Sigmoid volvulus without gangrene, and the operation for obstructing right colon cancer?
cards.a: Endoscopic detorsion with a flatus tube, then elective sigmoid colectomy; obstructing right-sided cancer gets right hemicolectomy with primary anastomosis.

cards.q: Paralytic ileus after surgery with low potassium: first treatment? Ogilvie's drug of choice?
cards.a: Correct the potassium and use drip and suck; for Ogilvie's, intravenous neostigmine with cardiac monitoring.
